info.text:
Why does the biggest squirrel pay 90% less per acorn?

Economies of scale: fixed costs get spread over more units, so cost per unit falls.
Made-up example: a $100 tree plus a $1 sack per acorn. 10 acorns = $11.00 each; 1,000 acorns = $1.10 each.
Costco's net sales grew from $149.4B (FY2019) to $297.2B (FY2026), and volume plus $5.9B in membership fees let it profit on an 11.1% gross margin (FY2026) vs. Kroger's 22.9% (FY2025).
Past a point, size can push costs back up: diseconomies of scale.

Sources: Costco FY2026 10-K and results release; Kroger FY2025 results release.
News and education, not financial advice.
